Three Speculative Claims




    1. Features are the fundamental unit of neural
       networks. They correspond to directions.
       These features can be rigorously studied and
       understood.

    2. Features are connected by weights, forming
       circuits. These circuits can also be rigorously
       studied and understood.

    3. Universality: Analogous features and circuits
       form across models and tasks.

text:
What MechInterp Needs and What It Gives



   Method                  Needs                                   Gives you

   Probes                  activations + labeled examples          a cheap detector
   Steering / ablation     write access to activations             causal evidence, control
   Sparse autoencoders     activations + lots of compute           a dictionary of concepts
   Attribution graphs      replacement model + researcher time     explains one prompt
   NLAs                    a trained verbalizer                    readable hypotheses (may be wrong)


                     All of these need white-box access (weights or activations).
            Evidence is mostly existential (“we found X”), not universal (“there is no Y”).
                     Not finding a “deception feature” is weak evidence of safety.

General Patterns in Circuits

     • High-abstraction features in middle layers, simple token features in early/late
       layers
     • Attention moves most information in early layers
     • “Default” circuits that get overwritten (e.g. “unknown person” → specific person)
     • Multiple pathways/shortcuts to the answer
     • Computation on special token positions (e.g. full stops, <assistant:>)
     • Confidence-reducing features (cf. negative name movers in IOI)
     • Many “boring” features active but not part of the core computation
